headline: Approved variance for 5, 7, and 9 Wilson Road and three nonconforming house permits; continued 75 North Street and 31 Cedar Street hearings.
summary: The board approved a variance to subdivide a merged lot at 5, 7, and 9 Wilson Road. It approved special permits to expand or raise nonconforming houses at 7 Herbert Street, 37 Clark Street, and 26 Linden Street. The 75 North Street and 31 Cedar Street hearings were continued.
decisions: Continued the 75 North Street amendment petition to September 16, 2026, by a 4-0 vote.
Approved a variance for 5, 7, and 9 Wilson Road to subdivide a lot merged under common ownership, by a 4-0 vote, subject to 12 standard conditions.
Approved a special permit for 7 Herbert Street to reconstruct the rear addition and build a two-story rear addition, by a 4-0 vote.
Approved a special permit for 37 Clark Street for a covered porch and single-story addition six feet from the side property line, by a 4-0 vote.
Approved a special permit for 26 Linden Street to increase the house height from approximately eighteen feet to 24.5 feet, by a 4-0 vote.
Continued the 31 Cedar Street variance request to October 21, 2026, by a 4-0 vote.
Approved the minutes of the July 29, 2026 meeting as drafted, with all members in favor.

Location: 31 Cedar Street (Map 34, Lot 0052) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: 31 Cedar Street, LLC & Salem Residential Properties, LLC, through Michael 
Becker 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of 31 CEDAR STREET, 
LLC and SALEM RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTIES, LLC, through 
MICHAEL BECKER, at 31 CEDAR STREET (Map 34, Lot 0052) (R2 Zoning 
District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem 
Zoning Ordinance to permit the separate development of two existing record parcels; 
retain the existing two-family dwelling at 31-33 Cedar Street; and relocate the historic 
dwelling at 259 Washington Street to 27- 29 Cedar Street, retain the existing garage, 
and construct an addition to create a 2.5-story, two-family dwelling. Relief is requested 
for lot frontage, lot width, lot area, lot area per dwelling unit, lot coverage, and front 
and side setbacks at 31- 33 Cedar Street, and the same relief, together with rear setback 
relief, at 27-29 Cedar Street. 
 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney AJ Capano introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and describes the various 
components of the proposal, noting that it is a creative infill project, but that the centerpiece of the 
project is the preservation and adaptive reuse of a Salem historic building that would otherwise face 
demolition.  Mr. Capano indicates the Salem Historic Commission determined twice that the home 
that would be moved is historically and architecturally significant.  The Salem Historic Commission 
also signed a letter in support of the relocation of the house to Cedar Street, according to Mr. 
Capano.  He describes the architectural details of the home and also introduces Michael Becker as an 
accomplished developer in town with a history of preservation awards.  Mr. Capano also discusses 
the variance requests and the petition to subdivide the parcels that had merged previously under 
common ownership.  Mr. Capano states that the petition seeks to permit separate zoning along the 
existing parcel boundary and not create a new subdivision, while allowing the parcels to be 
developed separately based on the historical boundaries.  He also discusses the dimensional relief 
being requested and presents a dimensional table with further details about the proposal.  The 
revised plans show the complete project including the relocated house, addition, and parking spaces, 
according to Mr. Capano.  He also discusses the proposed easement that would allow one entrance 
from Cedar Street so that no additional curb cuts or loss of street parking would be necessary.  Floor 
plans and plot plans are shown, and Mr. Capano indicates that while the Board has not approved 
this petition in the past, the standards and law regarding variances and hardship have changed since 
then.  He contends that without the requested relief, there is no way for parcel two to be utilized, 
and that the proposal will not only preserve a historic home but also add two units of housing to the
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
September 9, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
  9 
community.  Mr. Capano acknowledges neighborhood concerns regarding parking and traffic and 
notes that six parking spaces are being proposed. 
 
Mr. Becker introduces himself and discusses the historic property at 259 Washington Street that is 
being proposed to be moved to Cedar Street.  He notes that it is currently out of place with the 
surrounding buildings, but has noteworthy architectural details.  Mr. Becker presents a street view of 
the home and discusses the property in more detail, noting that Historic Salem Inc. has stated they 
are in support of relocating the home, subject to ZBA approval. 
 
Sanir Lutfija introduces himself and discusses the architectural details and property conditions.  He 
presents images of Cedar Street where the home is proposed to be relocated.  Mr. Lutfija presents 
renderings of the proposal showing the addition and the relocated home.  Elevations are presented 
as well. 
 
Chair Vyedin asks clarifying questions about the subdivision and parcel history.  Mr. Capano 
discusses the title and deed history, leading to common ownership in 1919, and the historic property 
boundaries.  The Board and petitioners continue to discuss the concept of merger and subdivision, 
and whether the Planning Board would also require its own review.  They next discuss the shared 
driveway and easement, as well as setback relief, and determine that additional relief will need to be 
requested under Section 5.1.6.  The Board reviews the site plan, and the petitioners discuss 
additional details, including the proposed staircase locations. The Board discusses additional relief 
under Section 3.2.4-3.  Potential revisions to the proposal are discussed, including parking updates, 
the exact placement of the home, and other plan updates.  The Board members next discuss 
potential special conditions they might like to see.  
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comment. 
 
Kiley Fenner of 35 Cedar Street introduces herself and discusses difficulties with snow storage and 
parking in the winter.  Ms. Fenner also speaks against the expansion of the existing historic home 
and overall opposes the petition. 
 
Milo Martinez of 78 Washington Square introduces himself and states he would like to convey the 
Historic Commission’s findings on the demolition delay waiver that they denied a month or so ago.  
Mr. Martinez speaks to the uniqueness of the property and architecture, noting it is a gem of a 
craftsman-style house.  Mr. Martinez states the Historic Commission is interested in any attempts to 
preserve and save this building.  He also notes that Salem has a long history of relocating buildings. 
 
Erin Heenan of 6 Fairfield Street introduces herself and states she is behind the proposed lot and 
building/relocation.  Ms. Heenan expresses opposition to the petition and contends that there is no 
lack of use with respect to the land in question.  She states it has served as a two-family home for 
decades, and that any hardship is self-inflicted.  She agrees that the historic home is worth saving, 
but Ms. Heenan notes that the Historic Commission’s letter does not address the issues of 
subdivision, lot area, frontage, setbacks, or the number of dwelling units the district permits.  Ms. 
Heenan asks that the Board deny the petition. 
 
Sean O’Brian of 21 Cedar Street introduces himself and notes he also owns 23 and 25 Cedar Street.  
Mr. O’Brian states he is an abutter and opposes the petition.  He argues that the two parcels are one 
lot under the concept of merger and discusses the property’s history.  He also notes this is a
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
September 9, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
  10 
proposal to add a two-family home to a property that the Board approved for short-term rentals in 
2019.  Mr. O’Brian asks that the Board deny the petition. 
 
Jay Valatka of 40 Cedar Street introduces himself and states he is in opposition to the petition.  He 
argues there is a detriment to the health, safety, and welfare of the neighborhood if this petition is to 
be approved.  Mr. Valatka discusses concerns regarding congestion and density, as well as traffic and 
parking.  He also expresses concerns about the historic home potentially having asbestos or lead 
paint.   
 
Patricia MacDonald of 8 Fairfield Street introduces herself and explains she is a rear abutter with a 
retaining wall bordering the property in question.  Ms. MacDonald expresses concerns related to the 
retaining wall and its integrity, and how it would be impacted by construction work and the 
proposed relocation.  Ms. MacDonald notes that, in 1987, the ZBA expressed concerns about the 
retaining wall, and that now the wall is 39 years older.  She asks that if relief is granted, there be a 
special condition requiring a pre-construction structural survey of the retaining wall by a licensed 
engineer and a signed hold harmless and indemnification agreement placing the full repair and 
replacement cost on the applicant, executed before any site work begins. 
 
Chair Verdin gives the petitioner a chance to respond to the public comments.  Mr. Becker notes 
that the current parking is tandem parking, which the Salem ordinance does not allow, but that this 
would be corrected under the proposal, and so argues that one nonconformity will be eliminated.  
He also contends that the project has been very well thought out and that he would be amenable to 
a special condition of having an asbestos survey of the property prior to the move.  Regarding the 
retaining wall concerns, he states he would be willing to discuss measures to fortify the wall with Ms. 
MacDonald. 
 
The Board members continue to discuss the petition and potential subdivision, noting a desire for 
the petitioner to address snow storage concerns in any plan revisions as well as updates with respect 
to parking.  Mr. Postich clarifies that the Board cannot technically vote to subdivide a lot, but it can 
provide dimensional relief for the subdivided lots.  
 
The petitioner requests to continue to the next regularly scheduled meeting of the ZBA in October. 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. McGaha motions to continue the petition of 31 CEDAR STREET, LLC 
and SALEM RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTIES, LLC, through MICHAEL BECKER, at 
31 CEDAR STREET (Map 34, Lot 0052) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 
Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to permit the separate development of 
two existing record parcels; retain the existing two-family dwelling at 31-33 Cedar Street; and 
relocate the historic dwelling at 259 Washington Street to 27- 29 Cedar Street, retain the existing 
garage, and construct an addition to create a 2.5-story, two-family dwelling, to the October 21, 2026, 
meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals. 
 
Mr. Larrick seconds the motion.  The vote is four (4) in favor (Ellen Simpson, Stephen Larrick, 
Christa McGaha, and Nina Vyedin) and none (0) opposed.  The motion passes.
